title: Copy scan of a captured suffix
statement: Let $L>0$, let a machine have $L+1$ work tapes, let $q_c,q_r$ be states, and let $f$ be a Boolean map. Suppose that in state $q_c$ the machine reads the last tape: on a symbol $b$ it writes $f(b)$ on tape zero, blanks the last tape, moves both heads right, and remains in $q_c$; on a blank it makes no writes, moves both heads left, and enters $q_r$. For Boolean words $\mathit{pre},\mathit{old},\mathit{rest}$, start with the heads at position $|\mathit{pre}|$, tape zero storing $\mathit{pre}$ followed by $\mathit{old}$, and the last tape storing $\mathit{rest}$ starting at position $|\mathit{pre}|$ with all earlier cells blank. After $|\mathit{rest}|+1$ steps the machine is in state $q_r$, the last tape is blank, tape zero stores $\mathit{pre}$ followed by the image of $\mathit{rest}$ under $f$ and then the suffix of $\mathit{old}$ after its first $|\mathit{rest}|$ symbols, and both heads are at position $|\mathit{pre}|+|\mathit{rest}|-1$.
hypotheses_covered: The specified transition rule in state $q_c$ for a symbol on the last tape
The specified transition rule in state $q_c$ for a blank on the last tape
replaced:
Consider a machine with at least two work tapes whose copy state, at a two-ended
configuration, overwrites the tape-zero cell with $f$ applied to the captured
symbol, blanks the captured cell, and advances both heads, exiting left into a
rewind state at the captured right blank. Starting with tape zero holding
$\mathit{pre} \mathbin{+\!\!+} \mathit{old}$, the capture tape holding
$\mathit{rest}$ beyond $|\mathit{pre}|$ already-erased cells, and both heads at
$|\mathit{pre}|$: after $|\mathit{rest}| + 1$ steps the machine is in the rewind
state, tape zero holds $\mathit{pre}$, then $f$ mapped over $\mathit{rest}$, then
the remainder of $\mathit{old}$ beyond position $|\mathit{rest}|$, the capture
tape is blank, and both heads stand at $|\mathit{pre}| + |\mathit{rest}| - 1$.
